meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Viet Nam (national jurisdiction, unitary state; no separate sub-state business registry)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (socialist-oriented market economy legal system; statutes and decrees prevail)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law on Anti-Money Laundering No. 14/2022/QH15 of 15 December 2022 (effective 1 March 2023), as implemented by Decree No. 19/2023/ND-CP of 18 April 2023; Circular No. 09/2023/TT-NHNN of 18 December 2023 (amended by Circular 04/2024/TT-NHNN) on AML/CFT in banking and payment services; Law No. 01/2020/QH14 on Enterprises of 17 June 2020 (effective 1 January 2021), Articles 4(4) and 6, and Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP of 4 January 2021 on enterprise registration, imposing UBO documentation obligations; Decision No. 05/2023/QD-TTg of 24 February 2023 on high-risk jurisdictions; Directive 07/VBHN-NHNN 2024 consolidating AML rules.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Business Registration Certificate of each direct foreign corporate shareholder (or parent entity)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Original country's company registrar (e.g., Companies House, ACRA, Delaware Division of Corporations) or as certified by the Vietnamese overseas trade mission
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for countries party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention (effective for Viet Nam since 15 July 2023); otherwise Consular Legalization at a Viet Nam Embassy/Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport or national ID copy of each ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) holding ≥25% and each legal representative / director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport/ID authority of the UBO's country of citizenship
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in the country of issue + Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization (for non-ASEAN/non-Hague states), followed by Vietnamese judicial record/notarized translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Judicial Record (Phiếu lý lịch tư pháp) obtained within 6 months for foreign legal representatives and UBOs
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent court/prosecution authority or national criminal records bureau of the person's country, legalized per authentication path
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization, then Vietnamese translation and notarization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Duly executed notarized foreign investment capital contribution commitment / Investment Registration Certificate (IRC) dossier and company lease agreement for the registered office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) of the province where the LLC is registered; notary office in Viet Nam
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic notarization at Vietnamese public notary; no apostille/consular step for domestically issued documents

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, legal representatives, and UBOs against: (i) the domestic Viet Nam PEP database and criminal records; (ii) the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list and the Viet Nam Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU, under the State Bank of Vietnam) official warning lists; (iii) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list for USD-denominated flows via Apple IAP / Google Play Billing settlement; (iv) EU and UK consolidated sanctions for international payment routing; and (v) the FATF grey/black list and Decision No. 05/2023/QD-TTg high-risk jurisdiction list. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) applies because the medium-risk enhanced voice-streaming sector accepts digital-first payment rails without face-to-face customer interaction; PEP status is presumed for Vietnamese state officials and their immediate family; screening must be repeated at least every 6 months or upon any ownership change.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Business Registration Portal of Viet Nam — Cổng thông tin quốc gia về đăng ký doanh nghiệp (https://dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn), operated by the Business Registration Management Agency under the Ministry of Planning and Investment; physical submission via the provincial Department of Planning and Investment (DPI).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The Vietnamese enterprise name must be written in Vietnamese using the Vietnamese alphabet, with digits and symbols; it must comprise two consecutive elements: (i) the legal form phrase ('Công ty TNHH' — limited liability company), and (ii) the proper name. Where the founding shareholder is foreign, the proper name may be transliterated into Vietnamese; an additional foreign-language name in Latin script is permitted if printed with smaller size lower in the Enterprise Registration Certificate, but the foreign name is not the statutory name for registration purposes and must not violate Decree 01/2021/ND-CP Articles 39-42. The English name of the LLC (e.g., 'Viet Nam ABC Voice Streaming Technology LLC') must be stated in the dossier as the translated name; it cannot replace the Vietnamese registered name. Transliteration must be non-deceptive and not identical or confusingly similar to any already-registered enterprise name, trade protected name, or well-known mark.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: *Government, Ministry, Bureau, State, Central, Provincial, People's Committee, Public Security — words creating confusion with state agencies (prohibited without a permit)

*Bank, Insurance, Fund Management, Securities, Payment Intermediary, Lottery, Gold, Foreign Exchange — licensed financial tokens requiring prior authorization by the State Bank of Viet Nam or Ministry of Finance before registration
*Vietnam/Vietnamese alone or 'National' implying governmental sponsorship where the enterprise is private
*Names identical or confusingly similar to an existing enterprise, historical heroes, government institutions, political organizations, social-policy organizations, or protected cultural names
*Words contrary to national traditions, ethics, or public order; obscene or offensive tokens
*Conjoined names of ministries (e.g., 'Bộ', 'Sở', 'Tổng cục') except where lawfully authorized by the competent ministry under Decree 01/2021/ND-CP Article 41
*Tokens implying an association, cooperative union, or public utility status that the LLC does not possess
*Foreign-owned media/broadcast terms (TV, Radio) that could trigger supplementary licensing under media law for a voice-streaming app
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection for name conflict or non-compliance, the applicant has the right to file a written appeal with the Director General of the Business Registration Management Agency or the provincial DPI under Article 64 of Decree 01/2021/ND-CP and the Law on Handling of Administrative Violations No. 15/2012/QH13. The SOP: (1) receive the DPI's written refusal stating the conflicting registration number or legal basis; (2) within 30 days from the refusal, may re-submit an amended name proposal on the National Business Registration Portal (no separate administrative fee for re-use of the same dossier identifier), and simultaneously request re-exam of the conflicting name if the conflict is deemed unlawful; (3) if re-submission is refused again, file a formal administrative complaint to the provincial People's Committee under Law No. 02/2011/QH13 on Complaints, or appeal in the Administrative Court; (4) the DPI must settle the complaint within 10-45 working days depending on complexity; (5) a name that is not objected to within the 3-working-day electronic processing window is deemed accepted; the portal reserves the name for the applicant for 30 days after issuance of the Enterprise Registration Certificate, after which the name is tied to the LLC's legal existence permanently until dissolution or name change. Note: Viet Nam does not maintain a stand-alone pre-incorporation name-reservation register; name clearance is obtained at dossier submission, and the 30-day window refers to the validity of the approved application before the LLC must complete the seal registration and bank opening procedures to avoid re-screening.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office (i.e., a postal-only address without a physical desk/lease in Viet Nam) is NOT permissible for the registered head-office address of a foreign-invested LLC. The Enterprise Registration Certificate requires the exact address of the LLC's head office 'tru sở chính' located in Viet Nam territory, with a legally valid lease or ownership certificate and payment of local business taxes. However, a licensed shared-space or serviced-office arrangement (coworking operator providing a dedicated room/desk and lease invoice) is accepted by most DPIs if accompanied by (i) the operator's business registration extract and (ii) a notarized lease/service agreement with a term exceeding the incorporation window. For an interactive voice-streaming app relying on remote developers, the registered office may host administrative/back-office functions only; the content/service servers may be cloud-hosted offshore, but the legal seat must be a verifiable physical location in Viet Nam staffed during working hours, and the app operator must be able to produce records at that address within inspection timelines.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High — quantified at 65%+ during the first 18 months for medium-risk-enhanced digital entertainment LLCs. The DPI, the General Department of Taxation, and the Ministry of Public Security (cybercrimes division) conduct unannounced on-site inspections to verify the head-office existence, staffing, financial records, and compliance with the Investment Law capital contribution timetable. Non-financial license requirement (metadata flags requires_statutory_license=false) does not eliminate inspection risk; tax authorities routinely inspect newly incorporated foreign-owned LLCs within 6-12 months to verify the 'commercial substance' for profit attribution and to confirm the voice-streaming revenue (Apple IAP/Google Play Billing) is booked locally.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Provincial Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) / State budget of Viet Nam
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under Article 33 of Decree 01/2021/ND-CP and Circular 04/2021/TT-BKHĐT on enterprise registration fees: VND 100,000 (~USD 4.30-4.60) for online filing; VND 200,000 (~USD 8.60-9.20) for paper filing

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarized Vietnamese translation and certified true-copy of foreign corporate documents (certificate of incorporation, UBO passports/passport copies, apostilled power of attorney)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark in Hanoi/Ho Chi Minh City: USD 15-30 per page for translation plus notarial fee of VND 10,000-50,000 per document (Circular 09/2015/TT-BTP)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille / Consular legalization procurement for each foreign shareholder and UBO document (per document, at diplomatic/consular fee schedule of the issuing state's competent authority plus courier)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent Apostille authority of the foreign country (e.g., U.S. Department of State / UK FCDO) or Viet Nam Embassy/Consulate where consular legalization is required
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Common-market benchmark USD 30-100 per apostille per document plus USD 25-50 courier and coordination fee; not a Vietnamese statutory tariff for foreign-issued documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Investment Registration Certificate (IRC) dossier preparation and legal counsel advisory retainer for foreign-invested LLC incorporation, including UBO chart, AML/KYC policy, and company charter draft
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External Vietnamese law firm / licensed legal adviser; DPI receives the statutory registration fee (the DPI fee for IRC issuance is VND 250,000 ~ USD 10.7, included in the retainer item)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for tier-1/boutique law firms in Viet Nam for a single-member/two-member foreign LLC with digital-services scope: USD 800-1,500 flat stage-1 fee (DTA/EVFTA structuring included)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO/AML enhanced due-diligence screening subscription (PEP list, UN/OFAC/EU/UK sanctions list, Viet Nam FIU high-risk list) for all corporate shareholders, directors, and UBOs covering the pre-incorporation window and first 6 months of operations
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial data provider (Refinitiv/World-Check), Vietnamese KYC/AML technology vendor, and the internal AML compliance officer
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market subscription benchmark USD 300-500 for medium-risk enhanced digital entertainment entity screening package covering unlimited name screening for 6 months

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office physical lease for the LLC head office — first 3 months deposit and notarization of the lease agreement (space sufficient for administrative seat requirement)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Lessor (licensed coworking operator or building owner) and Vietnamese notary public
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a serviced administrative office in Tier-1 cities: USD 250-350/month for a small office/desk bundle plus one-month deposit; VND 1 million notarization fee (approx. USD 40)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law on Enterprise No. 59/2020/QH14, Articles 75-77, 122 (limited liability companies); Law on Investment No. 61/2020/QH14, Articles 38-39 (investment registration procedures for foreign investors); Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP on enterprise registration; Decree No. 31/2021/ND-CP detailing the Law on Investment
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) of the province/city of the company's head office; for entities located inside an export processing zone or industrial park, the Management Board of the Export Processing/Industrial Zone has parallel authority to issue both the Investment Registration Certificate (IRC) and the Enterprise Registration Certificate (ERC)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Enterprise Registration Application in the form prescribed under Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP (Form MA-01) submitted via the National Business Registration Portal (https://dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn), together with the Investment Registration Proposal (Form A.I.1) submitted through the National Single Window Public Service Portal (https://dichvucong.gov.vn)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed for a pure digital voice streaming social platform under the Law on Enterprise 2020 and Law on Investment 2020. The subscribed charter capital is freely agreed by the members and must fully be contributed within 90 days from the ERC issuance date. For foreign-invested projects, the investor must evidence financial capacity (bank statements or audited financials) at the IRC application stage. Funds contributed must be remitted to the Vietnamese legal entity's corporate bank account; an escrow arrangement is not mandatory but is commonly used in practice for inter-member capital commitments.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: General Department of Taxation (Tổng cục Thuế) of the Ministry of Finance, Socialist Republic of Vietnam; central administrative and filing portal: https://etaxvn.gdt.gov.vn (e-tax portal for tax declaration, assessment and payment); electronic invoice system portal: https://hoadondientu.gdt.gov.vn; national business registration portal: https://dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn; official English portal: https://www.gdt.gov.vn
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Obtain an Investment Registration Certificate (IRC) for the foreign-invested project from the provincial Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) or the industrial-zone/EPZ management authority under Law on Investment No. 61/2020/QH14 and Decree No. 31/2021/ND-CP. Step 2: Apply for enterprise registration via https://dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn to obtain the Enterprise Registration Certificate (ERC); under the integrated one-stop mechanism of Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP, the enterprise code stated on the ERC is simultaneously the Tax Identification Number (MST / TIN). Step 3: Within 10 working days of ERC issuance, submit Tax Registration Declaration Form 01-ĐK-TCT through the e-tax portal https://etaxvn.gdt.gov.vn; the competent tax authority issues the Certificate of Tax Registration and opens the taxpayer account, which automatically registers the LLC for Value Added Tax (VAT, credit method), Corporate Income Tax (CIT), Personal Income Tax finalization duty, and electronic invoice obligations. Step 4: Register the electronic invoice template with the local tax office and activate the certified e-invoice application under Decree No. 123/2020/ND-CP and Circular No. 78/2021/TT-BTC. Step 5: Open a foreign-currency and Vietnamese-dong settlement account at a licensed bank in Vietnam, notify the tax authority of the banking details, and obtain the customs/import-export code if the entity undertakes cross-border movement of goods; the foreign-invested LLC receives a single consolidated tax code covering VAT, CIT, and related sub-codes for the head office, branches, and participating operations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: the foreign-invested LLC is a Vietnamese resident enterprise under Law on Corporate Income Tax No. 14/2008/QH12 as amended, taxed at the entity level on worldwide income at the standard CIT rate of 20%; the owners do not file Vietnamese individual income tax on LLC profits and no pass-through or transparent treatment is available
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Vietnam has no IRS-style check-the-box or hybrid transparent-entity election. The LLC is mandatorily an entity-level CIT taxpayer and VAT registrant. Statutory elections available: (i) VAT method election — an enterprise with annual revenue from sale of goods/services of VND 1 billion or less may elect the Direct Method (VAT payable at 1% to 3% of turnover) instead of the Credit Method; however, LLCs with full accounting books and invoices are required to apply the Credit Method; (ii) CIT incentive election — the taxpayer may elect to apply preferential CIT rates (10% or 17%) and exemption/reduction schedules for qualifying software production, high-technology, data-processing/hosting services (relevant to ISIC 6311), subject to the roadmap conditions in Decree No. 218/2013/ND-CP and Circular No. 96/2015/TT-BTC; (iii) investment incentive elections — new investment projects may elect between different CIT incentive roadmaps (2-year exemption and 4-year 50% reduction, or 4-year exemption and 9-year 50% reduction in qualifying zones/sectors); (iv) transfer-pricing documentation status election — filing of Form LT-STP-LTP, Form TP-01, and related elections for country-by-country reporting thresholds under Decree No. 132/2020/ND-CP; (v) hybrid mismatch alignment — no elective deduction is permitted for hybrid mismatch arrangements; interest expenses exceeding 30% of earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) are non-deductible under Decree No. 20/2017/ND-CP as amended by Decree No. 68/2020/ND-CP
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification_note: Resident LLC is separate and distinct from its foreign shareholders; distributions of after-tax profits are not subject to additional Vietnamese CIT or dividend withholding tax under domestic law; the LLC ring-fences offshore shareholders from Vietnamese direct tax on the entity's retained earnings

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT / GTGT) under Law on VAT No. 13/2008/QH12 as amended by Law No. 31/2013/QH13 and Law No. 106/2016/QH13, implemented by Decree No. 209/2013/ND-CP as amended by Decree No. 49/2022/ND-CP and Circular No. 219/2013/TT-BTC as amended by Circular No. 48/2023/TT-BTC; foreign digital service provider regime governed by Decree No. 85/2021/ND-CP
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: VND 100,000,000 in annual taxable turnover triggers compulsory VAT registration for household and individual businesses; a foreign-invested LLC must register for VAT from the moment of enterprise registration with no de minimis turnover threshold (effectively zero-threshold mandatory registration). VAT returns are filed monthly or quarterly depending on turnover; if output VAT in a period exceeds input VAT, VAT refund claims are processed under Articles 72-75 of Law on Tax Administration No. 38/2019/QH14
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing effective 1 July 2022 under Decree No. 123/2020/ND-CP and Circular No. 78/2021/TT-BTC. All sales invoices, including export invoices, must be issued through a certified e-invoice application connected to the GDT e-invoice portal. The application transmits invoice data to the tax authority in real time or within one working day; the GDT generates an invoice verification code (mã của cơ quan thuế) for consumer-facing e-invoices, and the code must be printed or digitally embedded on the invoice (digital stamping). Invoices for export of services may be self-issued without a tax-authority verification code when the taxpayer has registered the e-invoice template and the export conditions are met, but the un-coded invoice must still be transmitted to the GDT portal for data acceptance within the reporting period. API integration: the taxable person or its e-invoice service provider uses the published web-service API of the GDT e-invoice system (HoaDonDienTu.GDT.Gov.Vn) for template registration, invoice issuance, replacement, adjustment, cancellation, and encipherment; failure to transmit within the prescribed period results in rejection of the invoice code and imposition of administrative fines up to VND 20,000,000 per violation
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.cross_border_digital_service_note: Because the LLC supplies the voice-streaming app through Apple App Store and Google Play Billing, Vietnam-source sales made via these marketplaces trigger output VAT at 10%; the obligation may be shifted to the foreign platform under Decree No. 85/2021/ND-CP only where the non-resident platform is treated as the overseas supplier; the VN LLC must maintain separate domestic and export revenue ledgers, reconcile app-store country-of-sale reports, and record Vietnamese consumer app-purchase revenue as domestic taxable turnover
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.reduced_and_zero_rate_summary: 0% applies to exported goods and services and international transportation; 5% applies to specified essential goods and services; 10% is the standard rate applied to the LLC's voice-streaming, chatroom, virtual-gift, subscription, and advertising revenues unless the services qualify as exports consumed entirely outside Vietnam

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated export VAT status is available under Article 9 of Decree No. 209/2013/ND-CP as amended by Decree No. 49/2022/ND-CP and Section II.1, Article 9 of Circular No. 219/2013/TT-BTC. For the ISIC 6311 voice-streaming social application, the supply must satisfy all of the following evidential conditions: (i) the service is rendered to a foreign organization or individual that is not a Vietnamese resident (offshore end-consumer or the overseas app-store operator acting as distributor of record); (ii) the service is consumed wholly outside Vietnam, demonstrated by the end-customer's billing country, IP geolocation, SIM/device country codes, platform country-of-sale analytics reports, and the app's territorial terms of service; (iii) payment is received in a convertible foreign currency from outside Vietnam through a licensed bank, which includes remittances from Apple Inc., Apple International Distribution Limited, Google Ireland Ltd / Google Asia Pacific Pte Ltd after commission deduction, supported by platform payout statements; (iv) a written or electronic agreement exists with the overseas counterpart, including the Apple Developer Program License Agreement and Google Play Distribution Agreement; (v) the taxpayer retains documentation that the counterparty is non-resident (foreign corporate number, registered offshore office address, VAT/GST overseas registration); (vi) for services considered exported software/digital content, the LLC must maintain the IT service export dossiers required by Circular No. 48/2023/TT-BTC, including technical service descriptions and server logs evidencing offshore content delivery. Services supplied to Vietnamese resident end-customers, including in-app purchases made from Vietnamese App Store/Play Store accounts, cannot be zero-rated; such revenue bears 10% VAT. The LLC may reclaim input VAT and file for VAT refund of excess input tax where export zero-rated revenues exceed domestic taxable revenues, subject to quarterly or annual refund procedures and a pre-refund audit by the General Department of Taxation
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (electronically cleared through the VNACCS/VCIS customs system) for any embedded goods or hardware components

Bill of Lading / Airway Bill for goods, or a formal Services Delivery and Acceptance Certificate signed by the offshore customer or platform counterparty confirming that the streaming, chatroom, and virtual-gift services were fully delivered and consumed outside Vietnam

Inward Remittance Certificate (xác nhận giao dịch ngoại tệ) issued by a licensed Vietnamese commercial bank evidencing the actual receipt of convertible foreign currency from the offshore buyer or App Store marketplace into the LLC's Vietnamese foreign-currency account

Commercial invoice and the executed service or digital-content distribution agreement with the foreign purchaser of record (including Apple Developer Program License Agreement and Google Play Distribution Agreement)
Bank statements and foreign-exchange allocation records reconciling the specific imported foreign currency amount against each export invoice number and the corresponding VAT zero-rating period

Platform sales-analytics and geolocation evidence (country-of-sale reports, IP addresses, Apple Store and Google Play financial reports) demonstrating that customer consumption occurred outside Vietnam

Withholding tax or tax identification certificates issued by the foreign payer (e.g., IRS Form W-8BEN-E, Irish Revenue VAT certificate for Apple, Singapore IRAS certificate for Google) establishing the non-resident status of the counterparty
Export VAT zero-rate supporting ledger and export file index prepared in accordance with Circular No. 219/2013/TT-BTC and Tax Administration Law No. 38/2019/QH14
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The General Department of Taxation and Customs Administration jointly audit export zero-rating claims with heightened scrutiny on digital-service exporters using app-store distribution. Where the statutory documentation bundle is incomplete, fabricated, or where the remitted foreign currency is not allocated to specific export invoices, the tax authority retrospectively treats the revenue as domestic supply at 10% VAT, disallows the zero-rating, claws back any previously refunded input VAT, and reassesses the output VAT shortfall. Legal consequences under Law on Tax Administration No. 38/2019/QH14 and Decree No. 125/2020/ND-CP include: (i) late-payment interest at 0.03% per day on all underpaid amounts from the original statutory due date until full payment; (ii) a fine of 20% of the underdeclared/underpaid tax where the error was not fraudulent; (iii) a fine of 1 to 3 times the evaded tax amount for intentional tax evasion, with the multiplier depending on aggravating circumstances; (iv) administrative fines up to VND 60,000,000 for invoice and documentation violations; (v) suspension of the taxpayer's e-invoice verification code and removal from the e-invoice system; (vi) publication of the taxpayer on the public non-compliant taxpayer list; (vii) criminal prosecution for tax evasion under Article 200 of the Penal Code No. 100/2015/QH13 as amended, carrying fines of up to VND 20,000,000,000 and custodial sentences of up to 20 years for organized fraud, and penalties for money laundering under Article 324 where proceeds are disguised; (viii) retrospective clawback periods of 5 years for VAT underdeclaration and 10 years for tax fraud; and (ix) joint liability of legal representatives and tax-compliance officers where false certificates of offshore consumption were knowingly issued. If foreign currency export earnings are not repatriated to Vietnam within 180 days without an approved State Bank of Vietnam extension, the LLC is also exposed to foreign-exchange sanctions under Circular No. 15/2015/TT-NHNN as amended and Decree No. 88/2019/ND-CP, including fines and suspension of foreign-currency accounts
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.vietnam_vat_zero_rating_legal_basis_note: Circular No. 219/2013/TT-BTC Article 9.1(e) and Circular No. 48/2023/TT-BTC clarify that software and digital content supplied to offshore parties and consumed abroad are export services; the place-of-consumption principle requires clear evidence that the customer received the benefit of the service while located outside Vietnamese territory
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.refund_mechanics: VAT refunds on export zero-rating are processed quarterly for enterprises with export revenue exceeding VND 25 billion per quarter and undergoing a pre-refund audit, or annually for other exporters; refunds of input VAT can be claimed when cumulative input VAT not fully credited is at least VND 300,000,000, with the statutory review period of 90 days for qualifying exporters and 40 days for enterprises that are not subject to a customs audit, as provided under Articles 72-74 and Article 75 of Law on Tax Administration No. 38/2019/QH14
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.transfer_pricing_and_controlled_transact: The zero-rated export revenue remitted to the VN LLC by Apple/Google is a controlled transaction under Decree No. 132/2020/ND-CP; the LLC must prepare transfer-pricing documentation if the foreign integrated turnover exceeds relevant thresholds, and must apply the arm's-length principle to the 15% to 30% app-store commission deducted by the platform; failure to do so can result in retrospective CIT adjustments and interest running from the filing date

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Planning and Investment of the provincial business registration authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 calendar days after the fiscal year-end (by 31 March for calendar-year filers)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of VND 10,000,000–15,000,000 (USD 400–600) under Decree 122/2021/ND-CP; continued non-submission for two consecutive years authorises compulsory administrative strike-off under Law on Enterprises 2020 Article 40.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Business License Tax (Lệ phí môn bài)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Vietnam General Department of Taxation / provincial tax department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 January of each fiscal year; newly established entities are exempt for the first year and must pay from the second year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest of 0.03% per day on unpaid and late-paid amounts; administrative fine under Decree 125/2020/ND-CP ranging from VND 1,000,000 to VND 3,000,000 (USD 40–120), with persistent non-payment triggering enforced collection measures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Finalization Return (Tờ khai quyết toán thuế TNDN) and audited financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Tax Department under the General Department of Taxation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 March of the following calendar year (for fiscal-year filers using calendar year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative late-filing fines under Decree 125/2020/ND-CP up to VND 25,000,000 (USD 1,000) for delays exceeding 90 days; default interest at 0.03% per day on any underpaid tax; continued non-filing can lead to forced assessment and criminal exposure in egregious cases.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual submission of audited financial statements to the tax directorial office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Tax Department (attached to the CIT finalization package)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: With the CIT finalization return, i.e., by 31 March of the following fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Treated as failure to submit part of the tax finalization dossier; subject to the same late-filing and unreportable-interest sanctions as the CIT return, plus disciplinary fines of VND 2,000,000–5,000,000 (USD 80–200) for accounting violations under Decree 41/2018/ND-CP.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Any enterprise with foreign-invested capital is compulsorily subject to annual independent audit under Law on Accounting 2015, Article 37(1)(a), irrespective of scale; additional mandatory audit applies to public companies, credit institutions, and insurance firms. No separate revenue/asset threshold is imposed on the FDI entity itself.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Vietnamese Accounting Standards (VAS) as local GAAP; IFRS is permitted for consolidated reporting under Ministry of Finance Decision (as amended) but statutory standalone financial statements must be prepared under VAS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Vietnam imposes no standalone annual UBO confirmation. The Annual Enterprise Report under Law on Enterprises 2020 Article 32 must include the current list of members and beneficial ownership details. Any capital transfer or change in UBO must be recorded in the member register and notified to the business registration authority within 10 calendar days; the updated list of members is filed with the provincial DPI upon each transfer.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (with contribution amounts, capital transfer history, and ownership percentages)
Minute Book of Members’ Council and Board of Members resolutions
Capital Contribution and Transfer Transaction Register
Book of Copies of Company Documents and Notices

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250–600 per annum for a registered address and agent service in Ho Chi Minh City or Hanoi
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000–4,500 for a small- to mid-sized foreign-invested LLC with a voice streaming app business and full independent audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Standard CIT rate is 20%. Preferential rates: 10% for 15 years for qualified high-tech, software, and digital content enterprises (including online platform activities) in eligible zones or under incentive criteria; 15–17% for small- and medium-sized enterprises meeting specified thresholds. Tax holidays: 2–4 years full exemption followed by 4–9 years of 50% reduction for new investment projects in encouraged sectors or economically difficult areas.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 03/TNDN – Annual corporate income tax finalization return; submitted electronically via the Vietnam eTax Portal (etaxvn.gdt.gov.vn). Quarterly provisional returns use Form 01/TNDN via the same e-filing system.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with quarterly provisional payments and declarations)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual finalization return: within 90 days after the end of the fiscal year (e.g., by March 30 if fiscal year ends December 31). Quarterly provisional tax returns: within 30 days after the end of each quarter. The final CIT payment must be made no later than the finalization deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax ID (MST), enterprise name, registered address, industry code (ISIC 6311 / VSIC 6311), fiscal year, and IRC/ERC certificates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Vietnamese tax identification number of the foreign-invested LLC. Attach investment registration certificate and enterprise registration certificate details.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue from voice streaming subscriptions, virtual gifts, in-app purchases, advertising, and other business income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all revenue from Apple IAP and Google Play Billing gross proceeds before platform commissions. In-app digital purchases are sourced in Vietnam if consumption occurs via Vietnamese users. No revenue apportionment for DTA unless permanent establishment exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable expenses directly incurred in generating revenue, with proper VAT invoices and payment documents.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only actual, documented business expenses incurred by the Vietnamese entity. Commissions to Apple/Google are deductible as service fees if supported by valid invoices and have proper FCT withholding. Non-deductible items include unsubstantiated related-party charges, royalties without substance, and provisions not meeting legal conditions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income = revenue – deductible expenses + other taxable income; adjusted for CIT incentives and loss carryforward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Calculate loss carryforward up to 5 consecutive years. Apply incentive rates only if the company holds valid certificates (e.g., high-tech, software enterprise). Foreign investors may not offset offshore losses against Vietnam-sourced income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: [C] CIT payable and incentive schedule – Lines 6–10
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax amount at statutory or preferential rate, less provisional payments, resulting in final balance payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim preferential 10% rate or tax holidays by completing incentive schedules and attaching supporting certificates. If no incentive certification, apply 20% flat rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Mandatory disclosure of related-party transactions including value, method, comparables, and economic substance information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must be filed together with annual CIT return if related-party transactions exceed thresholds. Include the TP documentation database key and legal entity identifier of overseas affiliates.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: administrative fine from VND 5 million to VND 25 million; late payment interest 0.03%/day. Understatement: penalty 20% of understated tax amount. Tax evasion: 100–200% of evaded tax. Criminal tax evasion: fine up to VND 4.5 billion and/or imprisonment up to 7 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% corporate income tax on dividends distributed by a Vietnamese LLC to its corporate shareholder (dividends are paid from after-tax profits). Individual shareholders receiving dividends pay 5% personal income tax. Branch profit remittance tax: 0% for most sectors, but 5% may apply for certain natural resource activities.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply DTA reduced rates: (1) Obtain a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the shareholder's tax authority; (2) Provide TRC and beneficial ownership declaration to the Vietnamese LLC before making payment; (3) LLC submits Form 01/NTNN to the Vietnamese tax authority to claim treaty exemption/reduction; (4) Tax authority issues approval or the payer applies the treaty rate pending post-filing verification; (5) Retain all documents for 10 years. Key treaties: Vietnam–Singapore, Vietnam–Hong Kong, Vietnam–Korea, Vietnam–China, Vietnam–US. Dividend rates generally 5–10% depending on shareholding thresholds; interest and royalties 10% (US royalties 5-10%).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Foreign Contractor Tax (FCT): Royalty and technology transfer payments to non-residents are subject to 5% VAT + 10% CIT on the gross payment (or 10% CIT + 5% VAT depending on separate fees). Interest paid to non-resident lenders: 5% WHT (FCT). Treaty reduced rates: Interest – generally 10% (5% for certain financial institutions under some treaties); Royalties – 10% (5% under Vietnam–US for certain copyright/software payments). Reduced rates require TRC and beneficial ownership proof.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: VND 30 billion aggregate related-party transaction value, or VND 50 billion total revenue, or VND 3 billion value of related-party service payments/interest; however, all taxpayers with related-party transactions must complete Form 01/TKQ regardless of threshold. Local File and Master File required if thresholds exceeded. Country-by-Country Report filing applies for groups with consolidated revenue ≥ VND 18 trillion (approx. EUR 750 million).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Decree 132/2020/ND-CP requires that related-party transactions reflect actual commercial substance, not merely legal form. Tax authorities may disregard arrangements without economic substance (e.g., shell offices, back-to-back arrangements, no personnel/assets/risk). Functional analysis must demonstrate that the Vietnamese LLC performs material functions (development, marketing, customer service, content moderation, user acquisition) and bears real economic risks. Profit allocation must align with the value-contributing activities. The Global Minimum Tax (Pillar Two / QDMTT) applies to MNEs with global revenue ≥ EUR 750 million, imposing top-up tax to 15% effective in Vietnam from January 2024.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate underreporting of Vietnamese users' payments, omission of Apple/Google revenue reports, use of shadow bank accounts, or false expenses in the form of shell vendor payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penal Code Art. 200: fine up to VND 4.5 billion and/or imprisonment 6 months to 7 years. Administrative penalty: 100–200% of evaded tax plus interest at 0.03%/day. Tax authority may enforce asset freezes and VAT invoice cancellation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Legal representatives and beneficial owners are criminally liable if they knowingly orchestrate evasion. Directors may face imprisonment, travel bans, and personal civil liability for restitution of evaded taxes. Corporate veil may be pierced where the LLC is a mere instrumentality.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Booking excessive royalties or management fees to offshore affiliates, failing to demonstrate that the Vietnamese entity earns arm's length returns for its user acquisition, content moderation, and payment processing functions, or relying on one-sided results without benchmarking.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax authorities may recharacterize intercompany pricing, adjust taxable income upward, impose a 20% penalty on the additional underpaid tax, and assess 0.03% per day late-payment interest. For thin-capitalization (interest expense exceeding 30% of EBITDA), disallowed and reclassified. Documentation failures trigger fines up to VND 50 million.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve fraudulent TP policies can be held personally liable for penalties if they knowingly caused false filings. Criminal liability may attach under Penal Code for tax evasion if TP adjustments exceed thresholds. Travel bans and asset seizures possible during audit.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Withhold Foreign Contractor Tax (FCT)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Vietnamese LLC runs on Apple App Store and Google Play, where Apple/Google act as collection agents. If the LLC itself is the seller of record, no FCT applies to Apple/Google if they are treated as non-resident digital platform operators? No—if the LLC pays commission to Apple/Google, the commission is subject to FCT on the portion that is for services rendered outside Vietnam? Actually Apple/Google commissions for distribution/app store services are generally subject to Vietnamese VAT/FCT when the Vietnamese user downloads from Vietnam; but if Apple/Google are non-resident and the LLC is the seller of record, the LLC must withhold FCT on the service fee paid to Apple/Google? The treatment is controversial: many cross-border app companies treat Apple/Google as non-resident taxpayers and apply 5% FCT on the commission, or claim DTA exemption if no PE. The red flag is failing to address FCT on platform commissions, advertising services, or IT services from foreign vendors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Withholding agent is liable for unpaid FCT plus 20% penalty and 0.03%/day interest. If Apple/Google are treated as the seller and the LLC is merely reselling, the whole revenue may be reclassified as Vietnamese-source and subject to CIT. Penalties up to VND 100 million for incorrect withholding.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable if they knowingly fail to withhold. Criminal tax evasion charges may be brought if the failure is part of a scheme to reduce Vietnamese tax, leading to imprisonment and restitution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Registering the Vietnamese LLC without real office, full-time staff, bank accounts, or actual decision-making authority; channeling content licensing, marketing, and user payment activities through an offshore affiliate to strip profits out of Vietnam, while claiming the LLC has no permanent establishment or no taxable presence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Decree 132 and GAAR principles, the tax authority may disregard the entity or reattribute profits to the Vietnamese economic employer. Additional CIT up to 20% (or 100-200% if fraudulent), plus interest. The LLC may also face revocation of IRC/ERC for non-compliance with investment law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Shareholders/directors who intentionally maintain an artificial structure to evade tax may have the corporate veil pierced; they become personally liable for tax debts and penalties. Travel bans, seizure of personal assets, and criminal prosecution under Penal Code Art. 200 or Art. 217 (false registration) apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money Laundering / AML Red Flags in Voice Streaming
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Permitting users to purchase virtual gifts or credits via misused payment cards, laundering illicit funds through high-value virtual gift exchanges with cashback schemes, or facilitating third-party payments that hide beneficial ownership; failing to perform KYCC on streamers or payment recipients.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penal Code Art. 324: imprisonment 3–15 years and fines up to VND 5 billion for money laundering. Administrative AML fines under Decree 11/2023/ND-CP up to VND 500 million. The enterprise may be forced to terminate operations; licenses revoked.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers face criminal indictment if they knowingly allowed laundering activities. The corporate veil can be pierced for fraud, subjecting personal assets. Travel bans and extradition treaties with foreign authorities may be triggered.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: MNE group with consolidated revenue ≥ EUR 750 million using Vietnamese LLC as a low-taxed entity (e.g., effective CIT rate below 15%) and failing to file the QDMTT top-up return or pay the top-up tax in Vietnam.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Enforcement of 15% Qualified Domestic Minimum Top-Up Tax (QDMTT) under Resolution 711/2023/QH15. Penalties for non-payment: late-payment interest 0.03%/day and administrative fines. The parent jurisdiction may impose its own IIR/Pillar Two top-up if Vietnam does not collect.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for ensuring that the top-up tax is properly calculated and reported; failure can result in civil liability to the group, administrative fines, and travel restrictions pending resolution of tax debt.
